models.name: ARCleared
models.description: Cleared (paid) accounts-receivable items, one row per cleared customer line item, derived from BSEG/BKPF for customer accounts (KOART='D') that have a clearing document. THIS IS THE SOURCE FOR AVERAGE COLLECTION PERIOD / DAYS-TO-PAY: days_to_pay is pre-computed as clearing_date minus baseline_date, so average collection period by customer = AVG(days_to_pay) filtered to invoice lines (cleared_amount > 0). Use for how-fast-customers-pay analysis, collection-efficiency scorecards, and payment-behaviour trends. Complements ARAging (mv_fi_ar_aging), which covers what is currently UNPAID/overdue; this MV covers what has already been COLLECTED. India context: amounts are in company currency (INR); baseline_date is typically the invoice date and the clock for net-30/45/60 terms; the MSME Act's 45-day expectation makes days_to_pay a compliance-relevant metric. Only paid items appear — open invoices have no collection period yet. Always filter tenant_id.

columns.description: Cleared amount in company currency (INR), positive for the customer invoice (debit) line and negative for the offsetting payment line. Filter cleared_amount > 0 to isolate invoice lines for collection-period averages and to sum collected revenue.

columns.name: days_to_pay
columns.description: Pre-computed collection period in days = clearing_date − baseline_date for the line. AVG(days_to_pay) where cleared_amount > 0 gives the average collection period. Higher = slower-paying customer. Meaningful on invoice lines; ignore on payment (negative) lines.

columns.description: Billing document (SD invoice, VBELN) that originated this cleared receivable — from BSEG.VBELN, falling back to BKPF/BSEG AWKEY when the origin is a billing doc (AWTYP='VBRK'). JOIN to BillingFlat.billing_doc to trace a payment back to its invoice and sales order: 'is sales order X paid?' = find BillingFlat.billing_doc for that sales_order, then check whether those billing_docs appear here (paid/cleared) vs in ArAging (still open). models.name: CustomerAdvance
models.description: Customer advances / down payments RECEIVED (advance payment, advance from customer, down payment on account, customer prepayment, advance balance). THIS IS THE CUSTOMER side — money customers PRE-PAID us. For advances we PAID / GAVE to a VENDOR or SUPPLIER ('advance to vendor', 'advance payment to supplier', 'vendor down payment', 'advances we gave to vendors'), use VendorAdvance (mv_fi_vendor_advance) instead — NOT this table. This is the only correct table for CUSTOMER advance / down-payment questions — do NOT use ArAging (mv_fi_ar_aging) or CustomerCreditExposure for advances; ArAging's negative open_amount mixes credit memos and overpayments, and credit-exposure bundles bills of exchange. One row per OPEN (uncleared) customer special-G/L down-payment line item, derived from BSEG/BKPF for customer accounts (KOART='D') carrying special G/L indicator UMSKZ='A' (the SAP-standard customer down-payment indicator) with no clearing document yet. THIS IS THE SOURCE FOR 'advance payment list of customer with balance', 'advance payment received from customers', 'customer advance / down-payment balance', and 'advances on account' questions. advance_amount is sign-normalised so a received advance (credit posting, SHKZG='H') is POSITIVE; a customer's advance balance = SUM(advance_amount) per customer (positive = cash the company is holding against future invoices). For 'advance payment list of customers WITH balance', GROUP BY customer and keep HAVING SUM(advance_amount) > 0. Complements ArAging (mv_fi_ar_aging), which covers normal open receivables (what the customer still OWES); this MV covers what the customer has PRE-PAID. Once a down payment is cleared against the final invoice it leaves this MV. Down-payment REQUESTS (noted/statistical items, UMSKZ='F') are excluded because they carry no real balance. India context: amounts are in company-code currency (INR); customer advances sit as a current liability ('advance from customer') until adjusted against the tax invoice, and are GST-relevant (GST is payable on advances received for services). Always filter tenant_id. Refreshes every 1 hour. FRAUD / AUDIT — route parked-funds, stale-advance, unadjusted-advance questions here (advances long past posting_date never adjusted against an invoice).

models.name: VendorAdvance
models.description: Vendor / supplier advances / down payments MADE — money the company PAID to a vendor IN ADVANCE, before the goods/services invoice (advance to vendor, advance payment to supplier, advance paid to vendor, vendor down payment, supplier prepayment, advances we gave to vendors). THIS IS THE ONLY CORRECT TABLE for any 'advance to vendor' / 'advance payment to supplier' / 'vendor down payment' question; it is the VENDOR mirror of CustomerAdvance (which is advances RECEIVED from customers — do NOT use that for vendor-side questions). One row per OPEN (uncleared) vendor special-G/L down-payment line item, derived from ACDOCA (the S/4HANA universal journal) on the leading ledger (RLDNR='0L'); vendor lines are identified by a populated LIFNR (KOART is not reliably populated on ACDOCA in this lake) carrying special G/L indicator UMSKZ='K' (the vendor down-payment indicator used in this lake) with no clearing document yet (AUGBL empty). THIS IS THE SOURCE FOR 'list of vendors we gave advance payment to', 'advance payment to vendors with balance', 'vendor-wise advance / down-payment balance', and 'open advances paid to suppliers' questions. advance_amount is the signed local-currency amount (ACDOCA HSL); only the paid-out leg (HSL > 0) is kept, so it is always POSITIVE; a vendor's outstanding advance balance = SUM(advance_amount) per vendor (positive = money the company has prepaid and not yet adjusted against an invoice). For 'vendors WITH advance balance', GROUP BY vendor and keep HAVING SUM(advance_amount) > 0. For 'last 12 months' / a date window, filter on posting_date (e.g. posting_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 12 MONTH)). Complements ApAging (mv_fi_ap_aging), which covers normal open payables (what the company still OWES the vendor); this MV covers what the company has PRE-PAID the vendor. Once the down payment is cleared against the final invoice it leaves this MV. Down-payment REQUESTS (noted/statistical items, UMSKZ='F') are excluded. India context: amounts are in company-code currency (INR); advances paid to vendors commonly attract TDS deduction at the time of advance payment (u/s 194C/194Q etc.) and sit as a current asset ('advance to suppliers') until adjusted against the purchase invoice. Always filter tenant_id. Refreshes every 1 hour. FRAUD / AUDIT — route parked-advance, stale vendor-advance, and long-unadjusted-advance questions here (advances long past posting_date never adjusted against a vendor invoice).

Use this in preference to base tables (VBAK/VBAP/VBUK/VBUP/VBKD) for ANY question about sales orders, order value, customers, materials sold, order status, blocks or rejections. India context: net_value (NETWR) is in document currency — typically INR for domestic Indian orders; place-of-supply (intra-state CGST+SGST vs inter-state IGST) is determined at billing — this order view has NO region column, so join Customer on sold_to for REGIO; incoterms like 'FOB Mumbai' common. One row per sales-order line (sales_order + item). SCOPE WARNING: this is an ORDER-side view — it does NOT have invoice/billing fields like `invoice`, `invoice_created`, `billing_date`, `billed_qty`, `billed_value`, or delivery fields like `delivery`, `delivery_date`, `delivered_qty`. For invoice/billing fields join BillingFlat on `BillingFlat.sales_order = SalesOrderFlat.sales_order`. For delivery fields join DeliveryFlat on `DeliveryFlat.sales_order = SalesOrderFlat.sales_order`. (There is no ref_sales_order column and no O2cFlow / cycle-time-days model.) SAP TRANSACTION / REPORT CODE — route here if asked by code: VA05 / VA03 — list of sales orders.

models.name: DeliveryFlat
models.description:
Pre-aggregated/pre-joined materialized view. Use ONLY for shipment, delivery, goods-issue, picking, dispatch, or logistics questions. India context: inter-state deliveries trigger GST e-way-bill (>50k INR threshold); ship_to_region drives place-of-supply; route + vehicle_id feed e-way-bill Part-B. The delivered_qty column (sourced from LIPS.LFIMG / VBFA.RFMNG) is the GOODS-ISSUED quantity — i.e. how much physically left the warehouse. This is NOT a billing quantity, NOT an invoiced quantity, and NOT a sales-revenue quantity. If user asks about 'billed', 'invoiced', 'revenue', 'sales value', 'amount', or 'invoice qty' → DO NOT use this MV. Use BillingFlat instead. Use DeliveryFlat ONLY when the question is specifically about deliveries, shipments, GI dates, picking, dispatch, on-time delivery performance, freight, or open delivery backlog. SAP TRANSACTION / REPORT CODE — route here if asked by code: VL06O / VL06 — outbound delivery monitor.

SAP report codes routed here: VL06O (Outbound Delivery Monitor), VL10 (Delivery Due List).

models.name: BillingFlat
models.description:
Pre-aggregated/pre-joined materialized view. Use this in preference to base tables for ANY question about BILLED / INVOICED quantities or values — including 'billed quantity', 'invoiced qty', 'total billed', 'revenue by material', 'sales value', 'invoice value', 'amount invoiced', 'FKIMG', 'NETWR'. THIS IS THE TABLE FOR A 'SALES INVOICE REPORT' and its Indian-business synonyms — 'sales register', 'sales invoice list', 'invoice list', 'tax invoice', 'GST sales report', 'bill book', 'bill register', 'bill-wise sales', 'sales bill details', 'party-wise / customer-wise sales bills', 'item-wise sales' — all mean the list of customer billing documents and resolve to mv_sd_billing_flat. When a request is a bare 'report'/'register'/'list' with no explicit measure, default to one row per invoice line projecting billing_doc, item, billing_date, customer_name, material, material_desc, billed_qty, net_value (taxable value) and tax_amount (GST), filtered to the asked period and ordered by billing_date DESC; net out cancellations/credit memos via billing_type (S1/G2) when the user asks for clean sales. India context: net_value (NETWR) is in INR for domestic Indian invoices; the GST e-invoice IRN is generated against billing_type 'F2'; place-of-supply (intra-state CGST+SGST vs inter-state IGST) drives the tax_amount split. STATE / INTER-STATE: this MV carries `customer_region` (sold-to state, KNA1.REGIO) and `supplier_region` (plant state, T001W.REGIO) directly — use them for state-level revenue/GST analysis (no Customer join needed). `is_interstate` is a precomputed BOOLEAN (TRUE = inter-state/IGST, FALSE = intra-state/CGST+SGST, NULL = region unknown); for 'interstate sales / revenue %' use SUM(CASE WHEN is_interstate THEN net_value END)*100.0/NULLIF(SUM(net_value),0) — never reference a non-existent is_interstate='X' string or invent a region column. The billed_qty column (sourced from VBRP.FKIMG) is the canonical invoiced quantity per material per invoice line. The net_value column is invoiced amount in document currency. ONE ROW PER INVOICE LINE — for material-level totals always SUM(billed_qty). There is NO `is_cancelled`, `sign_factor`, `cancels_invoice`, or `posting_status` column; cancellations and credit memos are SEPARATE rows identified by `billing_type` (S1=cancellation, G2=credit memo, L2=debit memo) / `doc_category` — exclude or net them via `billing_type`, never via a non-existent flag. CRITICAL: NEVER substitute mv_sd_delivery_flat for billing questions. When user says BILLED, INVOICED, or REVENUE → always use this MV, never DeliveryFlat. GST / TAX (output): tax_amount (VBRP.MWSBP) IS the OUTPUT GST/VAT collected on each billing line (combined CGST+SGST intra-state or IGST inter-state — one combined figure, no separate CGST/SGST/IGST columns). This MV is the ONLY place GST is available at PRODUCT / MATERIAL / CUSTOMER grain — for 'GST collected / output GST / tax collected by product category / material / customer / sales org' use SUM(tax_amount) GROUP BY material_group / material / sold_to HERE. (mv_fi_tax_lines is G/L-grain only and carries no product.) Note: this line-grain output GST will not tie out exactly to mv_fi_tax_lines, which also includes input/manual/movement tax. FRAUD / AUDIT — route channel-stuffing, revenue-inflation, credit-memo-abuse, fictitious-sales questions here (period-end billing spikes netted by G2 credit memos next period).

SAP report codes routed here: VF05 (Billing Document List), VF04 (Billing Due List).

models.name: TaxLines
models.description: Tax (GST/VAT) postings derived from ACDOCA, PRE-AGGREGATED by company_code × fiscal_year × fiscal_period × posting_month × tax_code × tax_country × gl_account (it is NOT one row per accounting line). USE THIS in preference to ACDOCA for any GST/VAT/tax question. tax_amount is the net tax in INR (sign-normalised SUM of ACDOCA.HSL) — the GST/tax posted. Synonyms: GST / VAT / indirect tax. OUTPUT vs INPUT GST: there is NO tax_direction column — NEVER filter on one. Split by tax_code prefix instead: OUTPUT GST (collected on sales) = tax_code LIKE 'A%'; INPUT GST (credit on purchases) = tax_code LIKE 'V%' (V0 = exempt, V5/V12/V18/V28 = IGST slabs). Net GST payable for a period = SUM(tax_amount WHERE tax_code LIKE 'A%') − SUM(tax_amount WHERE tax_code LIKE 'V%') over the Indian fiscal period (Apr-Mar). NOTE (India): stores ONE combined tax amount per group — there is NO separate CGST / SGST / IGST / cess breakdown, so never invent cgst/sgst/igst columns; report total GST via tax_amount. There is also NO base/taxable-amount column (do not reference base_amount_local) — only tax_amount exists. GRAIN LIMIT — this MV is G/L + tax-code grain ONLY: it has NO product, material, material_group, customer, vendor, profit center, or cost center column, so NEVER join it to CSKS / MARA or invent a bridge column like cost_center. Use it for statutory / GL-grain GST totals: GSTR-3B, net payable, GST by tax_code / gl_account / company_code / tax_country / month. ROUTING — for 'GST COLLECTED (output GST) by product category / material / customer / sales org', do NOT use this MV; use the BillingFlat model (mv_sd_billing_flat) instead — its tax_amount is the output GST per billing line, so SUM(tax_amount) GROUP BY material_group / material / sold_to. Slice GST HERE only by columns that exist: tax_code, gl_account, company_code, tax_country, posting_month / fiscal_year / fiscal_period.

models.description: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source; also known as withholding tax / WHT) accounting lines from ACDOCA — covers Indian Income Tax Act sections 192, 194A, 194C, 194H, 194I, 194J, 194Q, 194R, 195. One row per TDS deduction or deposit posting. ALWAYS use this MV for TDS questions — NEVER query ACDOCA directly for TDS. The MV pre-filters to TDS payable GL accounts (range 0002701%) plus TDS receivable (0001903200), and derives the section from the SKAT account description. tds_status='DEDUCTED' = TDS booked as liability when vendor invoice is posted (credit side). tds_status='DEPOSITED' = TDS paid to government via challan (debit side). Grain: one row per tenant + company code + document + fiscal year + line. Time scope: monthly-partitioned by posting date; reversed documents excluded. Refresh: scheduled incremental every 1h.
